fact: National Hurricane Center, July 9, 2026: Tropical Storm Marisol has formed east of the Leeward Islands. It is forecast to become a hurricane on July 11 and to pass over the Bahamas on July 12 and 13.

National Hurricane Center, August 18, 2026: Tropical Storm Tobias has formed in the western Caribbean. It is expected to become a hurricane and to reach the coast of the Yucatan Peninsula near Cancun on August 21.

Lisbon, June 20, 2026: Portugal's air traffic controllers have announced a 48 hour strike starting at midnight on July 14. Most flights to and from Lisbon and Porto are expected to be canceled on July 14 and 15.

Meridian Air press release, August 5, 2026: The union representing our cabin crew has called a strike for August 12 and 13. We expect to cancel about half of our flights on those two days and will rebook affected passengers.

North Atlantic weather bulletin, September 2, 2026: Storm Ysolde has been named. Gales are expected across Ireland, Wales and western Scotland from the morning of September 4, and ferry crossings on the Irish Sea are likely to be canceled.
Rome, July 3, 2026: Italy's rail unions have called a 24 hour national rail strike from 9 pm on July 21 to 9 pm on July 22. Most high-speed and regional trains will not run.
National Hurricane Center, June 30, 2026: Tropical Storm Nadia has formed in the southern Gulf of Mexico and is expected to come ashore in Tamaulipas, Mexico, on July 2.
Northwind Airlines press release, July 15, 2026: The pilots' strike planned for July 24 has been called off after an agreement with the union. All flights will operate as scheduled.
Japan Meteorological Agency, August 24, 2026: Typhoon Kaori is expected to pass close to Okinawa on August 27 and 28. Flights and ferries in the Ryukyu Islands are likely to be suspended.
Athens, August 19, 2026: Greek ferry workers have called a 24 hour strike for August 27. Ferries between Piraeus and the islands will stay in port.
Paris, May 29, 2026: French air traffic controllers have called a strike for June 10 and 11, and flights across France are expected to be canceled.

Sentinel Wall, Cayo Brava, Honduras: a wall dive. The top of the wall is at 14 meters and it drops past 40 meters, so every dive on it goes deeper than 10 meters.
Parrotfish Garden, Cayo Brava, Honduras: a shallow reef dive for beginners. The reef lies between 4 and 8 meters, and no part of the site is deeper than 9 meters.
Tallow Gorge, Rio Cuyo, Costa Rica: a white-water rafting run with grade 4 rapids from start to finish.
Lantern Run, Rio Cuyo, Costa Rica: a family rafting trip on the lower river, with grade 2 rapids from start to finish.
Aerie Adventures, Interlaken, Switzerland: tandem paragliding flights from Beatenberg, landing in Interlaken.
Talon Excursions, Queenstown, New Zealand: jet-boat rides through the canyons of the Arrowmere River.
Blue Chimney, Cayo Brava, Honduras: a cavern dive that runs from 6 meters down to 16 meters.
Upper Rio Cuyo, Costa Rica: grade 5 rapids, run only by expert kayakers.
Glacier Air, Interlaken, Switzerland: helicopter sightseeing flights over the Jungfrau region.
Highline Canyoning, Interlaken, Switzerland: guided canyoning trips with abseils and jumps into pools.
